question: Does information-directed probe selection produce a better information state than uniform probing under an equal probe budget, when the returned observation must influence the next choice?
world: evaluate_bitstring semantics: hidden target t in {0,1}^L, probe q returns the exact score (L - d_H(q,t))/L; feasible set T(E) by archaeon.producer.fossil_inference (block solver, falsified against enumeration)

acquisition_objective.primary: ER(q|E) = sum_d n_d^2 / N: expected remaining feasible targets after observing q, under a UNIFORM prior over T(E) (a named indifference assumption, not a claim about the generator); minimise; exact integers, no enumeration of targets
acquisition_objective.ties: equal ER numerator = TIED; the class is recorded; the lexicographically smallest probe names the row
acquisition_objective.probe_pool: archaeon.producer.acquisition.probe_pool: every fossil, its complement, every single-bit flip of every fossil, the posterior mode and its single-bit flips, plus 32 uniform random probes (rng seeded per world/step); scored by ER alone; the pool is the scalable admissible set, and on L <= 8 worlds it reached the enumeration optimum class on >= 6 of 12 worlds (test)

arms.I: information-selected: at each step choose argmin ER over the pool built from the arm's CURRENT evidence; observe the exact score; append the fossil; recompute
arms.U: uniform: at each step draw a uniform random probe (the existing uniform policy); observe; append; recompute (U's evidence state is updated too, so the comparison is between selection rules, not between updating and not updating)

matching: same L, same hidden target, same initial evidence (one uniform random fossil -- the production reality: one fossil per landscape), same probe budget N_steps, same rng seed lineage per world; the arms' evidence states are separate objects and never share a returned fossil

worlds.initial_fossil: one uniform random candidate scored against the target

primary_information_metric: log2 |T(E)| after N_steps probes (lower is better); paired per world (I - U)
secondary_metrics: uniquely fixed bits at every step
probes needed to reach |T| = 1 (capped at N_steps + 1 if not reached)
immediate task score of each probe and its cumulative mean (SOLUTION vs INFORMATION progress)

per selected probe: Hamming distance to the nearest fossil (candidate diversity), number of distinct outcomes in its partition and its outcome entropy (outcome diversity), ER (information value), E[score] (immediate quality), fixed-bit increment realised (incremental constraint value)
diversity_test: Spearman rank correlation, per world-step over the whole probe pool, between candidate diversity (Hamming distance to the nearest fossil) and information value (-ER); reported per L as the median over world-steps with a bootstrap-free interquartile range; the claim 'diverse inputs produce diverse consequences' is judged by whether that correlation is materially positive (median rho >= 0.5) -- preregistered as a QUESTION, no direction assumed

licensing_threshold_preregistered.INFORMATION_SELECTOR_VALIDATED: for EVERY L in {8,12,16,24}: the paired mean of (log2|T_U| - log2|T_I|) at N_steps is >= 1.0 bit AND I <= U (log2|T|) on >= 24 of 30 seeds (exact one-sided sign test p < 0.001 at 30)
licensing_threshold_preregistered.NO_ADVANTAGE_OVER_UNIFORM: some L fails both clauses without I being worse
licensing_threshold_preregistered.INFORMATION_OBJECTIVE_MISALIGNED: I reaches a smaller feasible set but the realised fixed-bit count or identification steps are NOT better than U on any L (the objective moves the metric it optimises but not the decision-useful quantities)
licensing_threshold_preregistered.COMPUTATIONALLY_INTRACTABLE: any (L, step) selection exceeds 60 s wall time on this host
licensing_threshold_preregistered.REPRESENTATION_INSUFFICIENT: a contradiction arises from exact scores (would indicate a defect in the evidence representation) -- fail closed
licensing_threshold_preregistered.note: task score is measured and reported; it is NOT part of the licensing rule: an informative probe may score badly by design

stopping_rule: run every (L, seed) once; no re-runs; no seed selection after the fact
assumptions: uniform prior over T(E) for every expectation
the probe pool is the admissible set; a probe outside it is never chosen
exact scores (no noise): this matches the executor (BIT_DETERMINISTIC)
runner: scratch script archaeon/docs/h0h5/S3_SYNTHETIC_RUNNER_2026-09-12.py (committed beside this file); output S3_SYNTHETIC_RESULTS_2026-09-12.json
